weaknesses: The paper never says what the curve adds beyond the scalar endpoint. The matched rate min{1, d/[n log(ed)]} has the same order as the unrestricted scalar target in CausalSmithUnrestricted2026. The proofs also show V_{1/2}(P)=1/8+F_P(1/4), so the half-budget lower bound amounts to estimating the dual process at one fixed shadow price, which is an L1-distance problem. Fix: in the Introduction and Discussion, state plainly that the whole curve costs no more than its endpoint, which is the payoff of the factor-one dual contraction. Tone down the Discussion sentence 'The lower-bound experiment explains why capacity matters' and the claim that 'uncertainty about how to allocate limited capacity suffices', since the same difficulty already appears at b=1.

The estimator is described as a practical procedure, but its practical value is never discussed. K=max{2,floor(L/512)} equals 2 unless d>e^{1023}, so the Jackson degree is effectively fixed. H_0=4096 makes the pilot intervals cover almost everything at realistic n. The reported output is a conditional expectation over n! permutations and 2^n markings. Fix: add a paragraph after the estimator definition saying the constants serve the proof, that the rate is a theoretical benchmark, and how the conditional average would be approximated in practice (for example by Monte Carlo over the auxiliary draws). Move 'computational complexity' from a one-phrase future-work item into that paragraph.

The assumptions are stated but hardly discussed. Consistency is tautological under the observation map in synth_1, where Y is defined as Y(A). The dependence of C_epsilon and c_epsilon on overlap is not given; the proofs imply polynomial growth in 1/epsilon. The restrictions to a known alphabet, binary outcomes, and a fixed rather than shrinking epsilon are not interpreted. Fix: after the model-class definition, add a paragraph that explains each restriction, reports how the constants scale with epsilon, and says which conditions the lower-bound family uses (it uses propensity 1/2, so overlap does not bind there).

The literature positioning is thin and describes the key cited input inconsistently. JiaoHanWeissman2018 is called a 'two-sample L1 result' in the Introduction, a 'known-S bound' in the lemma proof, and a 'known-distribution L1 minimax result' in the fixed-alphabet proof, yet the locator cites the unknown-both-distributions reduction. Standard work on budget-constrained targeting (Bhattacharya and Dupas 2012) and on the non-regular optimal value functional (Luedtke and van der Laan; Hirano and Porter) is missing. Fix: use one accurate description of what Jiao, Han and Weissman supply, and add a short paragraph on non-smooth optimal-value estimation that explains how the finite-sample minimax view complements it.

The headline theorem repeats the full content of the capacity-active theorem (scalar estimator, occupied-cell effects, binding policy). It also adds a full-budget identity conditioned on b_0=0, even though that identity holds for every P regardless of b_0. Fix: reduce the matched theorem to the two-sided risk bound, point to the capacity-active theorem for the family properties, and state the V_1 identity as a separate remark without the b_0=0 condition.

The main-text setup is split into 11 'synth' definitions, several of which duplicate one another or appear after they are used. The reader has to reconstruct the model from scattered fragments. Fix: merge the cell mass, propensity, potential-outcome mean, treatment effect and control value into one 'Cell quantities' definition placed before the policy class. Merge the category-cell mass and four-vector arm-mass definitions into one, and drop the unused potential atom space.
defects: Text-mode math will not compile. 'Fix an endpoint parameter \ensuremath{b_0}\in[0,1/2]' and 'A shadow price \ensuremath{\lambda}\in[0,1]' put \in outside math mode. Rewrite as \(b_0\in[0,1/2]\) and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\).

Placeholder-style labels reach the reader. Environments are anchored as synth_1 through synth_11, and the text says 'The simplex in \cref{obj:synth_10}'. Give them descriptive labels, for example def:simplex and def:observation-map.

Several objects are used before they are defined. The paired-family definition uses 'the simplex' before the simplex definition appears. The budget-value definition uses I before the sentence that defines I. The control-value definition uses \mu_{0j} before the potential-outcome mean definition. The iid assumption uses 'observed margin' before the observation-map definition. Reorder each definition to come before its first use.

Near-duplicate definitions. The cell-mass definition (synth_2) and the product-law/propensity definition (synth_3) both define p_j. The category-cell mass definition (synth_8) repeats the prose definition of q_{ay,j} given before synth_9. The finite-sample definition (synth_11) repeats the O^{(n)} introduced in the setup prose. Merge them.
The potential atom space definition (synth_6) is never used. It also indexes cells as {j<d}, starting at 0, while the rest of the paper uses [d]. Delete it.

The consistency assumption 'Y=Y(A) almost surely' holds automatically, because the observation map defines the observed outcome as Y(A). Either define Y independently, or state that consistency is built into the observation map and drop the separate assumption.

The capacity-active theorem says 'every collection of observed-data laws satisfying \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling} for each full-data law', which is garbled. Replace it with 'under \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}'.
'The half-budget constraint is binding for P' in the capacity-active theorem is never defined. State it as the matched theorem does: there is \pi with \sum_j p_j\pi_j=1/2 that attains V_{1/2}(P).
The matched theorem bullet 'each occupied cell has p_j>0, \tau_j\in[1/8,3/8], and \tau_j>0' is redundant. Delete 'and \tau_j>0'.
The matched theorem states the full-budget identity only 'When b_0=0', but the identity is unconditional. Remove the condition.

In the fixed-alphabet proposition, the symbol c is used both for the risk constant ('constants c,C') and for the common effect ('If some c>0 satisfies \tau_j=c'). Rename the effect, for example to \gamma as in the proof.
The symbol \Pi is overloaded: \Pi_b(P) is the policy class, while \Pi_{[r,s]} is the clipping map in the estimator. Rename the clipping operator, for example to \operatorname{clip}_{[r,s]}.
The symbol B is overloaded: B(P) is the control value, B is a generic bound in the two boundedness lemmas, and B_j is the bad-pilot score. Use M or \bar B for the generic bound.

Verification jargon appears as if it were mathematics: 'Uniform process handle \mathsf H_{n,d}', 'belonging to the uniform process handle', and the label thm:integrated-process-certificate. Rename to 'process bound constants' and state the bounds directly.
The subscript in \mathsf H_{n,d} is misleading, because the definition requires membership 'simultaneously for every n,d'. Drop the subscript.

Lean artifacts appear in lemma statements and proofs. The maximal-bound lemma says 'let n,d be nonnegative integers, let \epsilon\in\mathbb R'. The empirical-process lemma allows 'any real overlap parameter \epsilon' and invokes the 'convention x/0=0'. The capped-count identity proof says 'When d=0, there is no probability law...'. The curve upper-bound proof mentions 'the complete-lattice convention'. Restrict to the paper's parameter range and delete the degenerate-case remarks.
The empirical-process boundedness lemma asserts only that a continuous function on [0,1] is bounded. Fold it into a one-line remark.

Vacuous clauses in the estimator's final step: 'If an implementation stores an optimizer, it stores the least element of the nonempty compact argmin set' and 'These branch rules ... apply under every data or treatment-effect tie'. The output does not depend on an optimizer, so delete both.
The dual-representation proposition says 'Let P be a full-data causal law with observed margin'. The clause 'with observed margin' asserts nothing; delete it.
The integrated-process theorem mixes scales: bias and good-pilot bounds are stated at the nL scale, the bad-pilot bound as 'C_\epsilon d/(mL)'. State all bounds at the nL scale.
The fixed-alphabet proof calls the cited input 'the known-distribution L1 minimax result', while the locator cites the unknown-both-distributions reduction. Make the description match the locator.
The dual-process definition g_a(u) depends on \epsilon, but the notation hides this dependence. Write g_a^{\epsilon}, or state the dependence in the definition.
The budget policy class definition does not quantify b or P inside the environment. Add 'For b\in[0,1] and a law P with cell masses p_j'.
The overlap assumption uses \epsilon without stating its range, which appears only in the prose afterwards ('where 0<\epsilon<1/2'). Move the range into the assumption.

Structural problem: the unnumbered '\section*{Appendices}' is followed by the section 'Proofs and verification scope', and then the main proofs appear later in a separate section, 'Proofs of the main results'. Put the main-result proofs first, or merge the two sections under one clear heading.

weaknesses: The contribution relative to Jiao–Han–Weissman and to the self-cited scalar result is under-argued. The estimator's practical content is conceded only in passing. K=max{2,⌊log(ed)/512⌋} stays at 2 unless d>e^{1023}, and H_0=4096 makes the pilot intervals almost vacuous. Several prose claims are stronger than or unsupported by the formal statements. Fix: delete the ε-dependence claim or prove it, and qualify the post-selection sentence.

The assumption discussion does not address restrictiveness. Fix: in the setup and limitations, state that the procedure takes ε as a known tuning input. Discuss continuous or bounded outcomes and discretized covariates, and interpret the fixed-overlap restriction relative to the rare-cell regime the paper advertises.

Nonregularity and ties get only one sentence ('permit multiple maximizing policies'), even though Hirano–Porter and Luedtke–van der Laan are invoked as the relevant literature.
